---
title: "How did the first flight compare?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

The first flight of the corrected glider, filmed and measured, against what this
chapter predicted for it.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
**Flight video `IMG_1665.mov`** · filmed by the user, 2026-08-31 · the glider as
flown carries the euro 50 cent, not the 1p. Read off the video: it decodes at
640 × 360 and 30 fps; the glider leaves the hand at frame 100 and is lying still
on the grass by frame 156; its wingspan measures 20 px across when at rest,
read off a 12× crop with a 5 px rule.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed
The camera's **horizontal field of view is 66°**, typical of a phone's main
lens, which is what converts pixels to metres — nothing in the video states it.
The glider is assumed to **lie broadside** at rest, so its measured span is not
foreshortened; the fuselage is visibly shorter than the span in those frames
even though it is longer in fact, which is what a fuselage pointing away from
the camera looks like. **Release height 1.5 m**, from the video: eye level, arm
extended, level push.
:::

```{python}
FPS, WIDTH_PX, HFOV = 30.0, 640, 66.0
F_RELEASE, F_DOWN = 100, 156          # last frame in hand / first frame at rest
SPAN_PX, SPAN_ERR = 20.0, 2.0         # apparent span at rest, and its read error
H_REL = 1.5                           # m, release height

# Pixels to metres: a span of S metres at range d subtends f*S/d pixels.
f_px = (WIDTH_PX / 2) / np.tand(HFOV / 2)
t_aloft = (F_DOWN - F_RELEASE) / FPS
rng = f_px * b_proj / SPAN_PX
rng_err = rng * SPAN_ERR / SPAN_PX    # one pixel of read error, propagated
v_avg = rng / t_aloft

# The aircraft as flown: the 50 cent in place of the fitted 1p.
m_flown = 0.016 - 3.56e-3 + 7.80e-3
x_flown = neutral_point() - 0.10 * c_w
t = trim(m_flown, x_flown)
a_stall, CL_max = stall(t["V"])

V_stall = (2 * m_flown * 9.81 / (1.225 * S_w * CL_max)) ** 0.5
rng_floor = V_stall * t_aloft         # it cannot have flown slower than this
rng_trim = t["V"] * t_aloft           # what the model's own speed implies
pred_rng, pred_t = t["LD"] * H_REL, H_REL / t["sink"]

# The same airframe at the balance point it was built with, for contrast. Its
# stall must be read at its own trim speed, not at the flown one.
heavy = trim(0.016, x_flown + 0.015)
heavy_past = heavy["alpha"] - stall(heavy["V"])[0]
```

**Answer.** It flew as designed. The glider was airborne for
`{python} f"{t_aloft:.2f}"` s against a predicted
`{python} f"{pred_t:.2f}"` s — agreement to
`{python} f"{abs(t_aloft-pred_t)/pred_t*100:.0f}"`% — and covered
`{python} f"{rng:.1f}"` ± `{python} f"{rng_err:.1f}"` m against a predicted
`{python} f"{pred_rng:.1f}"` m. Time is the number to trust here: it is counted
in frames and needs no camera calibration, whereas range rests on a
`{python} f"{SPAN_PX:.0f}"`-pixel measurement and an assumed lens.

**It was not thrown.** @fig-flight shows a level push at eye height with the arm
extending — the release the glide prediction assumes, not a hard overarm throw.
That matters, because it is what makes the comparison fair; an earlier read of
this same video as a hard throw was wrong, and the wide frames are what settle
it. There is no zoom, no ballooning and no pitch oscillation after release,
which is what an over-speed launch produces and which would be plainly visible.

**On launch speed.** The video cannot measure it directly — the glider's
attitude changes faster than its range does, so apparent span is unusable in the
first half-second — but it is boxed in tightly from both sides. It cannot have
left the hand below the stall speed of `{python} f"{V_stall:.1f}"` m/s or it
would have dropped, and the absence of any phugoid rules out much above trim.
**Launch was therefore at essentially the trim speed,
`{python} f"{t['V']:.1f}"` m/s** — which is exactly what a level hand push
should give, and why the flight settled immediately instead of hunting.

**The one inconsistency, and what it means.** The measured range implies an
average speed of `{python} f"{v_avg:.1f}"` m/s, which is *below* the
`{python} f"{V_stall:.1f}"` m/s stall — physically impossible for
`{python} f"{t_aloft:.2f}"` s of steady flight. So the range is underestimated,
not the model overestimated: flight time alone puts the floor at
`{python} f"{rng_floor:.1f}"` m, and the model's own trim speed over the
measured time gives `{python} f"{rng_trim:.1f}"` m, within
`{python} f"{abs(rng_trim-pred_rng)/pred_rng*100:.0f}"`% of the prediction. Two
pixels of span at rest is all it takes; that is the measurement to improve, and
a metre rule laid on the grass would remove the assumed lens entirely.

The glide itself is clean (@fig-flight, third panel): wings level, dihedral
holding, no wing drop, no mush. That is the corrected balance doing its job —
the same aircraft at its as-built balance point was predicted to trim
`{python} f"{heavy_past:.1f}"`° past the stall and to do none of those things.

```{python}
#| label: fig-flight
#| fig-cap: "Four frames from the flight. The release is a level push at eye height, not a throw. Circles mark the glider where it is small: in the glide, and at rest on the grass."
import matplotlib.image as mpimg

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 1.3))
ax.imshow(mpimg.imread("chapters/02-mceagle-300/flight-2026-08-31.png"))
ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-flight
#| tbl-cap: "Measured against predicted. Time aloft is counted in frames; range depends on the assumed lens and a 20-pixel span, and carries the uncertainty."
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame({
    "": ["time aloft", "range", "average speed", "launch speed",
         "trim speed", "stall speed"],
    "predicted": [f"{pred_t:.2f} s", f"{pred_rng:.1f} m",
                  f"{t['V']:.1f} m/s", f"{t['V']:.1f} m/s",
                  f"{t['V']:.2f} m/s", f"{V_stall:.2f} m/s"],
    "measured": [f"{t_aloft:.2f} s", f"{rng:.1f} ± {rng_err:.1f} m",
                 f"{v_avg:.1f} m/s", "not directly measurable",
                 "—", "—"],
    "note": ["frames counted, no calibration needed",
             f"floor of {rng_floor:.1f} m from time and stall speed",
             "below stall, so the range is low",
             "bounded to trim by stall and by no phugoid",
             "model, at the flown mass and balance",
             "model, at CL max"],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```
